title: Global economic stabilization remains fragile as geopolitical risk, cost pressure, AI investment, and shrinking fiscal room pull in different directions
source_unit: World Economic Forum, Chief Economists' Outlook: September 2026
geography: Global economic outlook based on WEF Chief Economists Survey fielded 4-20 August 2026, with regional comparisons

denominator.unit: WEF Chief Economists Survey response frame

outlook_weaken.unit: percent expecting global economic conditions to weaken over the next 12 months, down from 89% in May

inflation_rise.unit: percent expecting global inflation to rise over the next 12 months, down from 94% in May

resilience_improve.unit: percent expecting the global economy to become more resilient over the next 12 months

geopolitical_uncertainty.unit: percent selecting geopolitical conflicts among top five sources of global economic uncertainty

observations.method: WEF survey of chief economists conducted 4-20 August 2026, with historical comparison to earlier editions and supporting macroeconomic analysis.
observations.uncertainty: Expert expectations are not forecasts with known probabilities or realized outcomes; sample composition, question framing, and rapidly changing geopolitical conditions affect comparability across editions.
observations.subgroup: Chief economists from public and private sectors, with regional outlooks for major world regions and economies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Improving sentiment can coexist with severe household or regional stress; lower inflation expectations do not imply lower price levels or restored purchasing power.

observations.period: August 2026 survey; AI investment and data-centre social trade-offs

denominator.unit: WEF Chief Economists Survey response frame

ai_adoption_increase.unit: percent expecting AI adoption to increase over the next 12 months

ai_productivity_gains.unit: percent expecting AI to unlock meaningful productivity gains

data_center_growth.unit: percent expecting data-centre investment to contribute significantly to global growth

data_center_job_gap.unit: percent not expecting data-centre investment to create comparable numbers of jobs

local_pushback.unit: percent expecting data-centre expansion to face significant local-community pushback

observations.method: WEF expert survey on AI adoption, productivity, data-centre investment, employment, and local response, interpreted with the report's infrastructure and growth analysis.
observations.uncertainty: These are expectations rather than realized investment, productivity, employment, electricity costs, or local political outcomes; data-centre effects vary by location, ownership, grid conditions, and labor market.
observations.subgroup: Chief economists, AI and data-centre investors, workers, local communities, utilities, governments, and firms exposed to automation or infrastructure demand.
observations.counterinterpretation: Limited direct job creation can coexist with productivity, tax, construction, or supplier benefits; local opposition may demand better siting and cost allocation rather than reject AI entirely.

denominator.unit: WEF Chief Economists Survey response frame on household expenditure and real incomes

food_cost_increase.unit: percent expecting household food expenditure to increase

electricity_cost_increase.unit: percent expecting household electricity expenditure to increase

transport_cost_increase.unit: percent expecting household transport expenditure to increase

likely_policy_responses.value: tax reductions on essential goods 60%, consumption subsidies 54%, price caps 50%

regional_real_income_pressure.value: weakest real-income expectations were concentrated in the Middle East and North Africa, Europe, and Latin America and the Caribbean

observations.method: WEF survey of chief economists on expected household expenditure, real incomes, and likely government responses, supplemented by regional analysis.
observations.uncertainty: Expert expectations do not measure actual household budgets, incidence, policy implementation, or whether subsidies and price controls improve real purchasing power without other trade-offs.
observations.subgroup: Households, consumers, governments, essential-goods markets, and regions with differing real-income outlooks.
observations.counterinterpretation: Expected cost increases can accelerate substitution, efficiency, and energy transition; broad visible policies may protect households while creating fiscal, supply, or distributional complications.

observations.period: August 2026 survey; trade fragmentation and regional resilience

denominator.unit: WEF Chief Economists Survey response frame on trade, investment, and regional growth

fragmentation_increase.unit: percent expecting geoeconomic fragmentation to deepen over the next year

global_trade_increase.unit: share expecting global trade volumes to increase

china_non_us_exports.unit: percent expecting Chinese exports to markets outside the US to increase

regional_strong_growth.value: 74% expected strong or very strong growth in India and 73% in South-East Asia; 61% expected weak or very weak growth in Europe

fdi_increase.unit: percent expecting global foreign direct investment to increase

observations.method: WEF chief-economist survey on trade, investment, business environments, regional growth, and geoeconomic fragmentation.
observations.uncertainty: Expectations do not establish realized trade or FDI flows, tariff incidence, supply-chain relocation, regional welfare, or whether fragmentation produces durable strategic autonomy.
observations.subgroup: Chief economists, governments, multinational firms, regional economies, exporters, workers, and consumers exposed to trade and investment reconfiguration.
observations.counterinterpretation: Fragmentation can redirect investment and create new regional opportunities; rising trade volumes can coexist with higher costs, duplicated systems, and unequal bargaining power.

related_sources.claim: IMF World Economic Outlook provides complementary macroeconomic projections and inflation context.
WEF ASEAN Digital Economy Outlook provides a firm and infrastructure-level route for the regional participation and digital-market claims.
WEF Global Risks Report 2026 provides complementary risk-perception context for geopolitical, technological, and societal pressures.

boundary: This record adds an expert-expectations macro route linking geopolitical uncertainty, fiscal capacity, cost-of-living pressure, AI investment, data-centre infrastructure, trade fragmentation, and regional resilience. It uses the WEF Chief Economists Survey and report synthesis, not household-level inflation, realized trade flows, causal AI productivity, local political outcomes, or a forecast with known probabilities.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official WEF Chief Economists' Outlook September 2026 page and linked PDF were retrieved and reviewed for survey timing, outlook changes, resilience, geopolitical uncertainty, AI/data-centre expectations, household-cost pressures, trade fragmentation, and regional growth.
